# STEP 1 — Master Directory Structure & Shared-Utilities Strategy

## Project Layout (Vite, Vanilla ES Modules)

```
<workspace-root>/
├── index.html                    # Single Vite entry; mounts the active game into <div id="app">
├── package.json                  # deps: three (+ vite as devDependency). Nothing else.
└── src/
    ├── main.js                   # Entry point. Resolves ?game=<name> (default = first built game),
    │                             #   instantiates its Game class, owns mount/unmount lifecycle.
    └── shared/                   # ── Reusable across the entire collection ──
        ├── core/
        │   ├── GameLoop.js       # Fixed-timestep accumulator (120 Hz logic substeps) inside a clamped
        │   │                     #   frame delta; exposes setTimescale(t) — hit-stop is just timescale.
        │   ├── InputManager.js   # Unified dual-input: WASD/arrows + Gamepad API polled per-frame,
        │   │                     #   normalized to the same axis/button abstraction both games consume.
        │   └── StateMachine.js   # Tiny typed state machine (menu → playing → paused → gameover) shared by all games.
        ├── rendering/
        │   ├── RendererFactory.js# WebGLRenderer + perspective camera + resize handling, ACESFilmic tone mapping.
        │   ├── PostFXStack.js    # EffectComposer: RenderPass → UnrealBloomPass (tuned, see below).
        │   └── ProceduralTextures.js  # Canvas-API texture factory: glow sprites, grid floors, gradients — zero image files.
        ├── vfx/                  # The six required shared VFX systems
        │   ├── ParticleManager.js# Centralized pool; single InstancedMesh draw call; HARD CAP 500 live particles.
        │   ├── CameraShake.js    # Trauma-based: addTrauma(Δ) on impact ∝ velocity, decays over time, drives camera offset.
        │   ├── HitStop.js        # Brief timescale dilation (e.g. 1 → 0.05 for 80–120 ms), routed through GameLoop.setTimescale.
        │   ├── ShockwaveRings.js # Pooled expanding emissive rings on impacts/deaths; scale+fade, then return to pool.
        │   ├── MotionTrails.js   # Ring-buffer ribbon trails (instanced quads) for fast movers only — velocity-gated.
        │   └── FloatingText.js   # DOM-based glassmorphism score popups + optional 3D sprite variant; pooled, never re-created.
        ├── audio/
        │   └── SynthAudio.js     # Web Audio API: oscillator+envelope SFX voices and a small generative music sequencer.
        │                        #   Lazy AudioContext unlock on first input gesture (autoplay policy).
        └── utils/
            ├── MathUtils.js      # clamp, lerp, damp, randRange, angle helpers — the only math vocabulary shared code uses.
            ├── ObjectPool.js     # Generic acquire/release pool with pre-warm; every pooled entity implements reset().
            └── Disposer.js       # Centralized .dispose() walker for geometries/materials/textures on teardown — no leaks.

    └── [GameName]/               # Exactly one directory, created only when you name the game (STEP 2/3)
        ├── Game.js               # Orchestrator: owns scene, state machine, HUD, audio; implements start/pause/dispose.
        ├── config.js             # All tuning constants for that game in one place.
        ├── [Game]Scene.js        # Procedural world build (geometry displacement via noise/sines), MeshStandardMaterial only.
        ├── Entities/…            # Game-specific pooled entities (projectiles, pickups) — hand-written physics, no wrappers.
        └── HUD.js                # Glassmorphism overlay wiring: score, lives, state screens.
```

## Import Map (who pulls from whom)

- `main.js` → `[GameName]/Game.js` only. The game never imports across games; the shared layer is the sole cross-game surface.
- `[GameName]/*` → `shared/core`, `shared/vfx`, `shared/rendering`, `shared/audio`, `shared/utils`.
- `shared/*` modules import **only** from `three` and sibling `shared/` files — zero game knowledge, fully reusable for the rest of the collection.

## Key Architectural Decisions (fixed now, honored by every game)

1. **Deterministic core loop.** Fixed 120 Hz logic substeps inside a clamped frame delta; hit-stop is implemented as `GameLoop.setTimescale(t)` — one mechanism serves both physics stability and the required timescale dilation VFX.
2. **Pooling everywhere.** Projectiles, particles, rings, trails, floating text all pre-allocated via `ObjectPool` with `reset()` contracts. Zero allocation in the hot loop; zero GC hitches mid-game.
3. **Bloom tuned to glow, not wash out.** `UnrealBloomPass` at threshold ≈ 0.6, strength ≈ 1.1–1.4, radius ≈ 0.35, with ACESFilmic tone mapping and emissive-intensity discipline (emissives pushed past ~2.0 only on deliberate emitters).
4. **Memory ownership is explicit.** Every texture/geometry/material has one owner; `Disposer.js` walks the scene graph on unmount and calls `.dispose()` explicitly — verified, not assumed.
5. **PBR-only materials** (`MeshStandardMaterial`) with procedural Canvas textures for albedo/emissive/roughness where needed.

## Compliance Statements

- **Anti-Lazy Directive:** Every function in every file will be fully implemented and production-ready. No `// ... rest of the function`, no stubs, no "previously defined" elisions — a method that is called must exist on the module it's imported from, verified against what was actually written.
- **Strict Memory Management:** Explicit `.dispose()` via centralized ownership + `Disposer.js`; hard 500-particle cap enforced inside `ParticleManager` (requests beyond the cap are dropped oldest-first, never allocated); `InstancedMesh` for particles and trails; pooled everything else.
- **Sequential Output Protocol:** I will not generate ahead of your triggers — STEP 2 (`plan.md`) only on "Begin [Game Name]", STEP 3 only on "Plan approved". If any file truncates mid-write, I stop cleanly at the cut point and resume from the exact character when you type "continue", with no preamble.
